status: Colour sets. 2026-11-10: seven rules so every domain stays distinguishable and looks like its four-letter name, whatever the set's inspiration (Garrett: "Lime, Fire, Blue, Jade, Ruby, Gold, those must be distinguishable and have rules that govern the territory of their regions in color space; it must be obvious to the player based on a connection between their look and their four letter name"), three styles (Photic, Nocturne, Nacre), Dart Frog and Nacre re-derived under them, Nocturne's Gold rim moved 4 degrees so the HUD reads it as Gold, the vision sets re-balanced so their HUDs read for their own viewers, and worked examples the /colour-set skill teaches from. Nocturne is the game's default palette (Garrett, 2026-11-03); Dart Frog is proposed for the paid track; Nacre (2026-11-08) is the light set. The six-family truth in colour_domains.json is untouched; its anchors are read from PhoticColorSetSO.
maker: python3 Tools/Build/colour_set_maker.py (atlas, sample, fit, preview, hero); the /colour-set skill
space: OKLab, x = [L, a, b] of the sRGB colour (Bjorn Ottosson 2020)
rule: TWO-PIGMENT DOMAINS. A domain is two regions, its rim pigment (the prism's fresnel edge, the trail, the HUD, the signals) and its face pigment (the prism's body, most of what a player sees of it). A pigment is one paint seen from shadow to highlight: lighting scales a colour's linear RGB, which moves it along a ray from black in OKLab, so a pigment is the cone segment of colours with L0 <= L <= L1 whose chroma direction (a/L, b/L) lies within rho of (sat cos hue, sat sin hue). THE SEVEN RULES: (1) the band: any two pigments of different domains are at least margin apart in OKLab; (2) lighting-proof: their chroma directions are at least pigment_gap apart beyond their rho (no light or shadow turns one domain's pigment into another's); (3) form: a domain's rim and face differ in mid lightness by at least min_lightness_contrast (and in hue by min_hue_contrast, where a set or style asks for it); (4) the name: every rim reads as its own family of the colour_domains.json truth, clear of the band, as its swatch, as LIGHT (its centre ray at brightest channel 1: the prism's edge, the crystals) and as PAINT (the same numbers read as sRGB: the HUD, the score panels and the vessel tails read TrailHighlightColor that way), and Lime's rim also at the free crystal's body brightness; (5) communication, for a set made for a vision: as that viewer sees the painted colours, rims (as light and on the HUD), faces and each rim against its face stay vision_margin apart; (6) the voice: each face is its family's colour (its swatch rests in its family), its rim's own paint (its direction inside the rim's cone), or quiet (its whole pigment at or below the night line, where the truth holds only Fire and Blue, so it reads as night under a rim that carries the name); (7) apart: as painted, every two rims stay rim_separation apart, as light and as paint. Rules 4 (its paint reading), 6 and 7 are typical-vision rules: a set made for another vision keeps rule 5 for its viewer and may waive them, each with its reason. A set may name a style and keep its rules too. Examples are worked sets the skill teaches from; they keep every rule and are never written to the game.

laws_why.night_line: Below OKLab L 0.40 the six-family truth holds only Fire and Blue: no Gold, Lime, Jade or Ruby lives there, so a face wholly below it cannot name another domain. Nocturne's faces reach L 0.37.
laws_why.rim_separation: 0.10 OKLab, five just-noticeable steps, between the two closest rims as the game paints them.
laws_why.crystal_body: DarkCTA, the free crystal's body (about 93% of it), is painted at half of the brightest channel (PhoticColorSetSO, Docs/PALETTE.md section 2.2).

photic.name: Photic
photic.idea: One paint per domain, the way the original palette defines the six territories: the rim is the paint in light, the face the same paint in shadow or a deeper tone of its own family, so every prism is one family at two lightnesses.

nocturne.name: Nocturne
nocturne.idea: Lanterns: each rim glows in its family's hue and carries the name; each face is a dark jewel of a contrasting hue, wholly in the night, all six faces in one night band so no body outshines another.

nacre.name: Nacre
nacre.idea: Pearl: soft bodies in each family's own colour under clearer rims of the same family, a small iridescent turn of hue between them; faces painted at mid L 0.50-0.74 so the gameplay bloom lifts them to pastel instead of white, rims a sheen (rim_brightness 0.5-0.85), not a glow.

prism_mapping.rim: SO_ColorSet DomainColorSet.InsideBlockColor and its shielded twins: the prism's fresnel rim (_BrightColor). 'Inside' is a legacy name for the rim (Docs/PALETTE.md section 2).
prism_mapping.face: SO_ColorSet DomainColorSet.OutsideBlockColor and its shielded twins: the prism's base face (_DarkColor).
prism_mapping.fire: Fire and Lime are not DomainColorSets: Fire is EnvironmentColors.Danger (the danger rim over the domain's shielded face), Lime is the CTA pair (BrightCTA rim, DarkCTA body). How a set paints them is an open decision (see open).

unity: Tools/Build/author_colour_set_assets.py writes each set as Assets/_SO_Assets/Color Palettes/<Name>ColorSetSO.asset (Dart Frog: DartFrogColorSetSO.asset). Examples are not written. Every field takes its hue from one pigment of its domain and keeps PhoticColorSetSO's alpha and tier whiteness; rim fields keep the original's (HDR) brightness, face fields take their face pigment's own lightness, scaled by the original's step between tiers; Danger wears the Fire rim, BrightCTA and DarkCTA both wear the Lime rim, ElementalCrystalColors are copied. --check fails on drift or on any field that lands in another domain's pigment. The default is the set named by ThemeManagerDataContainer.asset's ColorSet slot and by the prefabs that hold a palette directly (ThemeManager, ArkView, CodexView, ConfigureDomainColumn, ConfigureSeatPedestal); PhoticColorSetSO is the palette every field's tuning comes from.

dart_frog.name: Dart Frog
dart_frog.by: Garrett (Jade from his photo of a green-and-bronze Dendrobates auratus); the other five laid out under the same rules. Re-derived 2026-11-10 under the seven rules: every frog keeps its warning colour as the rim and its dark ground as a quiet face.
dart_frog.summary: Poison dart frogs warn with bright colour on a dark ground, and so does this set: each rim is a frog's warning colour (strawberry, bumblebee, acid lime, Garrett's mint, azure, orchid) and each face is that frog's ground taken into the night (denim, coal, oxblood, bronze, petrol), so the bright edge carries the domain's name. Blue is the Azureus, blue on blue: azure over cobalt, one family. Until 2026-11-10 the grounds sat at mid L 0.39-0.45, light enough to name other domains: a Jade prism read as bronze, a Blue one as forest green, a Gold one as indigo.

fire.inspiration: Oophaga pumilio 'Blue Jeans': a strawberry-red frog with denim legs, the denim taken into the night

gold.inspiration: Dendrobates leucomelas, the bumblebee frog: yellow bands on black; the yellow kept in Gold's window (hue 82-96) so the HUD reads it as Gold, not Fire

lime.inspiration: a dart-frog pairing: acid lime over an oxblood ground

jade.inspiration: Dendrobates auratus, green-and-bronze (Garrett's photo, the lab's picture): its mint as the rim and its bronze ground as the face
jade.photo_coverage: The photo's brightest mint (#ACE3C6, its brightest tenth) and median bronze (#693A1B) sit just outside Mint and Bronze; their clearer and darker neighbours (#8FD3B5, #4F2A12) are inside. The greyest mint lies in the truth's Jade/Lime band (rule 4), and the median bronze is at the night line, L 0.40 (rule 6).

blue.inspiration: Dendrobates tinctorius 'Azureus', the blue poison frog: a sky-blue back over cobalt legs, blue on blue

ruby.inspiration: a dart-frog pairing: orchid over a petrol ground

nocturne.name: Nocturne
nocturne.by: Claude, asked by Garrett for the most beautiful set it could make; Garrett made it the default on 2026-11-03 after playing it. 2026-11-10: its Gold rim moved 4 degrees toward yellow (hue 83 to 87) so the HUD reads it as Gold, not the Gold/Fire band; it is the model of the Nocturne style.
nocturne.summary: Every prism is a lantern. The rim glows in its family's own hue and carries the domain; the face is a deep jewel tone of a different hue, all six faces in one night-dark band (mid L 0.27 to 0.32, every face wholly below L 0.37) so no body outshines another and the bodies read as tinted glass. Rims sit at mid L 0.66 to 0.85. Its rules are the Nocturne style's: faces quiet, at least 90 degrees of hue from their rims, one night band.

nacre.name: Nacre
nacre.by: Claude, asked by Garrett for a pastel set to complement Nocturne and Photic; re-derived 2026-11-10 under the seven rules (Garrett: "much better at following the rules while maintaining ... the desire for a pastel version").
nacre.summary: The inside of a shell. Soft bodies in each family's own colour (shell pink, champagne, celadon, seafoam, powder blue) under clearer rims of the same family, with a small iridescent turn of hue between the two, the way nacre shifts. Faces sit at mid L 0.56 to 0.66 so the gameplay bloom lifts them to pastel instead of white, and rims are painted at 0.7 of Photic's brightness (rim_brightness), a sheen, not a glow. Ruby keeps the one clear jewel, an amethyst body under an orchid rim: the six-family truth gives every pale violet to Blue and every pale pink to Fire, so no pastel Ruby exists. Until 2026-11-10 Nacre's faces were pale pastels of other hues (a lavender Jade, a periwinkle Gold, a sage Blue), which named the wrong domains and bloomed to white.

blue.inspiration: a pearl's blue sheen: periwinkle over powder

protanopia.summary: Made for eyes without long-wave (red) cones. A protan sees two hues, blue and yellow, so each domain gets its own place on that axis and its own lightness: Fire's and Gold's faces, one just-noticeable step apart for a protan in Nocturne, become navy and steel blue. Re-balanced 2026-11-10: its HUD colours, which its viewer could tell apart by only 4.5 JND, are now 8.0 JND apart, and its Gold rim stays in Gold's window.

waive.voice: Made for a vision: its faces are chosen so its viewer tells the six domains apart by a prism's body alone (rule 5); giving each body its typical-vision family would cost that.
waive.paint: Its viewer reads the HUD by rule 5, which measures the HUD's colours as that viewer sees them; holding the HUD reading to its typical-vision family would cost that separation.
waive.apart: Rule 5 keeps its rims apart for its own viewer, as light and on the HUD; the typical-vision distance between them is not what it is made for.

open: Nocturne as the default leaves four things on Photic: vessel hull materials, rendered card art, the vessel studio's colours and the Amoebius launcher's accents (Amoebius itself reads the live palette since 2026-11-05). Its dark faces also darken the HUD shielded signal (Docs/PALETTE.md section 1).

Lime as the CTA pair: DarkCTA paints about 93% of a free crystal, so a face pigment there makes free pickups read as oxblood. The Unity asset keeps the CTA lime on both halves for now; the Lime face (Oxblood) has no field.

Fire as danger: danger is a shared rim over each domain's shielded face, so Fire's own face pigment (Denim) has nowhere to go in SO_ColorSet today. The Unity asset paints Danger with the Fire rim (Strawberry) only. In a light set (Nacre) the danger prism's body is pale, so its Fire rim is all that warns.

The vision sets (2026-11-05) are measured on the palette's colours before bloom and ACES, with the Machado 2009 simulation at full severity (protanomaly and deuteranomaly are the milder forms of the same loss). How they look in the game, and whether the low-vision model (chromatic contrast halved) matches players with low vision, is judged by eye and by players: an editor pass per set is owed. They are picked in the Profile's colour-set rail, which now pages through the whole catalog through its three tiles. Since 2026-11-10 rule 5 also measures the HUD's rims (the numbers read as sRGB).

The HUD, the score panels and the vessel tails read SO_ColorSet.TrailHighlightColor as sRGB, while the trail shader and ColorSetUITheme read it as light. Until one encoding is chosen, rule 4 holds every rim to both readings, which narrows Gold's rim to hue 82-96.

PhoticColorSetSO is measured, not defined: its Jade prism rim (InsideBlockColor, an azure) sits in the band between Jade and Blue (COLOR.md section 6, deferred), and its prism faces are its rims' paint in shadow. colour_sets.py --report prints it under the rules; nothing enforces them on it.

The five colour-blind sets waive rules 6, 7 and rule 4's paint reading, because those rules are typical-vision rules; holding each of them to a vision-aware voice rule (a body that names its domain as its own viewer reads names) is open.
No set has been judged in the Unity editor after 2026-11-10: the stills come from colour_set_maker.py's model of the block shader and the gameplay bloom.
